# Visual Studio Code Configuration (`.vscode/`)

---

> [!CAUTION]
> **Do not modify, rename, or delete files in this folder.** These files configure Visual Studio Code (VS Code) for your course. Changing them may affect editing, debugging, testing, or other development tools. If you accidentally change or delete files, see [Restore Accidentally Changed Files](#restore-accidentally-changed-files).

---

## Purpose

The `.vscode/` folder stores configuration files that help provide a consistent development experience across GC-STEM course repositories.

[**Visual Studio Code (VS Code)**](https://code.visualstudio.com/) is a free code editor used to write, run, test, and debug programs. When you open your course repository in VS Code, it automatically recognizes the configuration files in this folder.

These files help:

- Maintain consistent code formatting and editor behavior.
- Recommend extensions that support course activities.
- Configure tools for running, debugging, and testing code.

The settings are maintained by GC-STEM. You may customize your personal VS Code preferences without changing these shared files.

## Check Your Development Environment

The [**`check_dev_env.py`**](https://github.com/GC-STEM/SOE/blob/main/scripts/python/check_dev_env.py) script in your shared **Standard Operating Environment (SOE)** checks whether key development tools are available.

It checks for CPython 3.12, GNU Bash, Git, GitHub CLI, and recommended SOE VS Code extensions. Results identify missing requirements and optional recommendations.

**Student action:** Run this read-only script anytime you want to check your development environment.

Open a terminal in your **course repository's root folder** and run the command for your operating system.

**Linux / macOS (Bash or Zsh)**:

```shell
python3 ../_shared/SOE/scripts/python/check_dev_env.py
```

**Windows (Git Bash or PowerShell 7+)**:

```shell
python ../_shared/SOE/scripts/python/check_dev_env.py
```

These commands assume your course repository and SOE were installed in the standard `~/Repos/` directory structure during setup.

Review the results. If the script reports missing requirements or errors, follow your course setup instructions or contact your instructor.

## Folder Contents

### `extensions.json`

Lists recommended and discouraged VS Code extensions. **Extensions** add features such as Python support, code formatting, spell checking, and diagram editing.

**Student action:** Follow your course setup instructions to install recommended extensions. Do not edit this file.

### `launch.json`

Configures the VS Code **debugger**, which helps you find and fix programming errors using breakpoints and step-by-step execution.

**Student action:** Use the debugger as instructed in your course activities. Do not edit this file.

### `mcp.json`

Configures **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** servers that can connect compatible AI tools to external services. No MCP servers are currently configured.

**Student action:** None. Do not edit this file.

### `settings.json`

Defines shared VS Code settings for code formatting, indentation, automatic saving, file associations, Markdown editing, and other editor features.

**Student action:** None. Use your personal VS Code user settings for individual preferences.

### `tasks.json`

Defines reusable VS Code **tasks** that run predefined commands, such as installing repository validation dependencies and checking repository configuration.

**Student action:** Run only when instructed. Do not edit this file.

### `README.md`

This document explains the purpose of the `.vscode/` folder and its contents.

**Student action:** Read for reference. No changes are needed.

## Help and Support

If VS Code does not behave as expected, follow your course's [Setup Tasks](https://github.com/GC-STEM/crs000/wiki/1%E2%80%901-Setup-Tasks) or contact your instructor. Do not attempt to fix configuration problems by changing these files unless instructed to do so.

### Restore Accidentally Changed Files

If you accidentally change or delete files in `.vscode/`, open a terminal in your course repository's root folder and run:

```shell
git fetch upstream main && git restore --source=upstream/main --staged --worktree -- .vscode/
```

This restores the original tracked files from your course's master repository, including deleted files. **Any changes you made to those files will be lost.** Files you added yourself will not be deleted.

This command assumes you completed the course setup tasks and configured the `upstream` Git remote. If the command fails, ask your instructor for help.
